name: Norwegian Refugee Council: programmes (charityevals' estimate)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: NRC's 2025 project revenue by country office (Annual Accounts 2025, note 2: NOK 7,276m over 39 country offices, NORCAP, regional offices and Norway left out), as the spread of its programmes; the branches' results aren't split by country, so this weights every country by its spending (Ukraine 13%, Sudan 11%).
summary: The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) spent NOK 8.7 billion ($837 million) in 2025 helping people displaced by conflict and disaster in 39 countries, mostly with government and UN grants: cash and vouchers (two fifths in Ukraine, a quarter in Sudan), food security, shelter, education, water and sanitation, legal assistance and protection for 10.6 million people, plus 613 NORCAP expert secondments to UN agencies and governments. NRC counts the people each programme reached and the cash it hands out, but publishes no controlled evaluation of its own, so the cash transfers count in full and every other part, built from spending, reach and the research on its kind of work, is counted at half by the shared missing-data slider. It comes to about 0.20 years of healthy life per $1,000 (combined range 0.05-0.80): cash carries about 35%, education's later earnings about 30%, food security about 15%, shelter, water and sanitation, legal assistance, NORCAP and protection the rest. NRC is phasing out food security by 2027, so a dollar given now buys a little more cash and less food security than in 2025; the biggest uncertainties are how much emergency education raises later earnings and how much of a crisis's excess deaths basic-needs aid averts.

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.label: Spending on the modelled programmes, 2025 (US$)
rows.formula: lfs_spend + shl_spend + edu_spend + wsh_spend + icl_spend + pfv_spend + csh_spend + nor_spend
rows.explainer: Every direct programme line of the 2025 accounts but advocacy and information (NOK 255.8m), which is charityevals' NRC advocacy model (norwegian-refugee-council-charityevals-advocacy): NOK 7,678.9m. NRC delivers itself in 38 programme countries; 5.7% of implementation went through local partners (Annual Report from the Board, p. 32).

rows.label: Total costs, 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: All costs: direct humanitarian costs, project support (NOK 470.6m), administration (NOK 71.0m) and fundraising (NOK 224.2m). They include NOK 229m of donated services (pro bono, mostly media space and consultancy, note 5), the donors' in-kind gift: counting them as cost is the same as leaving them out and lowering credit by their share of all resources (Convention 2).

rows.label: Direct costs on humanitarian activities, 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: The programme lines, NORCAP and advocacy and information (note 5's direct costs on humanitarian activities); project support is spread with administration and fundraising as overhead.

rows.label: Overhead multiplier (total ÷ direct programme costs)
rows.explainer: Spreads project support, administration and fundraising over the programmes in proportion to their cost, as GiveWell and ACE do: about 1.10.

rows.label: Livelihoods and food security: cost per person reached, with overhead
rows.explainer: Context: about $70 a person.

rows.label: NORCAP: expert assignments in 2025

source.title: Norwegian Refugee Council, Annual Report from the Board 2025 (published 18 June 2026)

rows.explainer: Assignments of NORCAP's roster experts to 48 organisations in 80 countries (UN agencies, the African Union, governments); 406 NORCAP experts were deployed at the end of 2025 (p. 45), so an assignment averages several months.

rows.label: NORCAP: cost per assignment, with overhead
rows.explainer: Context: about $120,000 an assignment, mostly the expert's pay, travel and support.

rows.label: Death rate among the people reached during the crisis, without the response
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.02 (0.012-0.04) a person-year: Sphere's emergency threshold is a crude death rate of 1 per 10,000 a day (0.037 a year); NRC's 2025 work ran from acute crises above it (Sudan, Gaza) to protracted ones close to the baseline (South Sudan, Ethiopia, Somalia, the DRC), so the average sits between. The same judgment as charityevals' Save the Children model for the same mix of crises.

rows.label: Death rate in the same populations before the crisis
rows.explainer: The crude death rates of three of NRC's largest African operations (Sudan, the DRC, South Sudan; UN World Population Prospects via the site's country facts), so only excess deaths count.

rows.label: Food security: share of the excess deaths the response averts among the people reached
rows.explainer: Judgment 2% (0.5-6%): food and cash for food in crises raise consumption, and some of the excess deaths are from hunger and its diseases, but NRC runs no nutrition treatment or health care, which avert most of a response's deaths. Reference class: charityevals' relief models take 0.75% for MSF's item distributions, 2% for ShelterBox's shelter, 3% for the American Red Cross's and 4% for Save the Children's response with health and nutrition.

rows.label: Years of the crisis the response covers per person
rows.explainer: Judgment half a year (3-12 months): distributions and cash usually cover a few months of a lean season or the first months after displacement.

rows.label: Food security: deaths averted per person reached (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Excess deaths over the time covered, times the share the response averts.

rows.label: Share of the deaths averted that are of children under five
rows.explainer: Judgment 45% (30-60%): in mortality surveys of crises the under-five death rate runs about twice the crude rate, and children under five are 17-20% of these populations, so they are 35-40% of all deaths and more of the excess ones (the family guide's 40-60%). The shared age splits (facts/death_ages.json) have no all-cause or crisis split for these countries (WHO's Global Health Estimates 2021 by age for Sudan, the DRC and South Sudan are where one would come from, for normal rather than crisis deaths); the three shares move the result by about 1%, so they stay ranged judgments, as in charityevals' other relief models.

rows.label: Of the deaths averted at five or older, share aged 5 to 14
rows.explainer: The relief models' shared figure (@death_ages.crisis_share_5_14_of_over5, 20%, 10-40%): most deaths over five in crises are of adults.

rows.label: Of the deaths averted at 15 or older, share aged 15 to 49
rows.explainer: Judgment 50% (30-70%); the rest at 50 and over, valued at GiveWell's 50-74 weight.

rows.label: Value of a crisis death averted (units of value)
rows.explainer: The site's one value of a death, by age band, times your value of a life.

rows.label: Food security: illness averted per person reached, in DALYs (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.0005 DALYs (0-0.002): acute malnutrition and its infections averted among those who don't die, beyond the consumption valued below; small because NRC's food support is a few months of food or cash, not treatment. About a fortieth of the branch's deaths and consumption value.

rows.label: Share of a programme line's spending that reaches people as cash, goods or materials
rows.explainer: Judgment 55% (40-70%): NRC's costs were 61% project materials and transfers, 37% salaries and 2% other (note 5: NOK 5,293m, 3,223m and 172m of 8,701m); the lines' own staff (distribution, engineers, trainers) take part of the rest. Used for food security, cash and shelter.

rows.label: US prices in 2017 relative to 2025
rows.explainer: Puts 2025 dollars into 2017 prices, the year of the PPP factors and the baselines.

rows.label: US prices in 2024 relative to 2025
rows.explainer: Puts 2025 dollars into 2024 prices, the year of Ukraine's consumption figure.

rows.label: Food security: cash, food and inputs delivered per person in the year (US$)
rows.explainer: The line's spending reaching people, per person reached: about $35. Counted in full as consumption: the deaths averted are a small share of the value (2% of excess deaths), so the overlap is negligible.

rows.label: PPP conversion (2017 international $ per US $), NRC's African crises
rows.explainer: The same three countries as the baseline death rate (World Bank, via the site's country facts).

rows.label: Consumption per person per year of the people reached in low-income crises (2017 PPP $)
rows.explainer: Judgment $700 PPP a year ($400-1,200): displaced and crisis-hit households in low-income countries, around the extreme-poverty line ($2.15 a day, $785 a year), as in charityevals' Save the Children model.

rows.label: Food security: ln(consumption) gain per person
rows.formula: years_exposed * ln(1 + value_delivered_per_person * cpi_2017_vs_2025 * ppp_factor / (baseline_consumption * years_exposed))
rows.explainer: The template's form: goods used up over the months they cover (years_exposed) raise consumption only in those months, so the gain is t × ln(1 + v ÷ (b × t)).

rows.label: Food security: gains to non-participants through local markets, as a share of the participants' gain
rows.explainer: A side effect: support to 1,140 bakeries in Darfur and South Kordofan helped halve bread prices for hundreds of thousands of buyers who aren't counted as reached (pp. 22-23), and cash spent locally raises traders' incomes; food bought in thin markets can also raise prices for others. The shared figure for cash spent locally, +10% (0 to +40%).

rows.label: Consumption per person per year of displaced people in Ukraine (2024 US$)
rows.explainer: Ukraine's household consumption per person from the national accounts, put on the household-survey scale by the site's shared ratio, times the recipients' share of the average.

rows.label: Displaced and war-affected recipients' consumption as a share of Ukraine's average
rows.explainer: The shared figure for displaced and frontline cash recipients in Ukraine (@ukraine.war_affected_aid_recipients_consumption_share, 70%, 50-100%).

rows.label: Cash: share of the 'Other' line handed to people as cash or vouchers
rows.explainer: Judgment 50% (35-71%): NRC transferred NOK 1,425m as cash and vouchers in 2025 across all its lines (p. 30); the multi-purpose and unconditional cash in the chart's split (62.7% and 9.2%, NOK 1,025m) sits outside the sector lines, 51% of the 'Other' line; the high end books all NOK 1,425m here (71%), the low end some of the multi-purpose cash in sector lines. The rest of the line is the cost of delivering the transfers and the line's share of country support (registration, screening, payment, monitoring, offices and security), counted at nothing as in the other branches: the report's examples of this line's work (rapid response in the DRC, Sudan's emergency response rooms, p. 31) are themselves cash transfers.

rows.label: Cash: transfer per person reached (US$)
rows.explainer: About $60 a person (an average household gets four or five times that).

rows.label: Cash: share in Ukraine

source.title: Norwegian Refugee Council, Annual Report from the Board 2025 (published 18 June 2026)
source.page: p. 30, Cash and voucher assistance (cash programming per country office)

rows.explainer: Ukraine's share of NRC's cash programming in 2025; Sudan 23.9%, Yemen 6.7%, the DRC 6.3%, the rest in low-income crises. Ukraine's recipients are far richer than the others, so their gain is computed at their own consumption.

rows.label: Cash: ln(consumption) gain per person
rows.formula: years_exposed * (csh_ukr_share * ln(1 + csh_transfer_per_person * cpi_2024_vs_2025 / (ukr_consumption * years_exposed)) + (1 - csh_ukr_share) * ln(1 + csh_transfer_per_person * cpi_2017_vs_2025 * ppp_factor / (baseline_consumption * years_exposed)))
rows.explainer: Each group's log gain at its own consumption over the months the transfers cover (years_exposed, the template's t × ln(1 + v ÷ (b × t))), weighted by its share of the money, taken as its share of the people. Ukraine's transfers per person are larger than elsewhere, so it has fewer of the people than of the money; at three times the amount per person the branch would be about 3% higher, so the approximation is kept.

rows.label: Cash: deaths averted per person reached (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Cash in the first months of a crisis buys food and health care like the food-security line, at the same share of excess deaths averted; none in Ukraine, where the war's excess deaths among civilians aren't from want.

rows.label: Shelter: value to households of in-kind shelter as a share of its cost
rows.explainer: The shared figure for housing and shelter given in kind (@aid_value.inkind_housing_vs_cash, 0.8, 0.6-0.95): households can't choose what they get and kits may not match needs; rental cash and repairs are worth close to their cost.

rows.label: Shelter: value of shelter and items delivered per person (US$)
rows.explainer: About $30 a person.

rows.label: Shelter: years the shelter or repair is used
rows.explainer: The shared figure for a crisis shelter programme's mix (@humanitarian_response.shelter_years_used, 2 years, 1-5): kits and tents are used up within about a year, repaired homes and schools last longer.

rows.label: Shelter: share in middle-income countries (Ukraine, Lebanon, Jordan, Colombia)
rows.explainer: Judgment 30% (15-45%): Ukraine (housing repairs and winterisation), Lebanon, Syria and Colombia are a large part of NRC's shelter work (country revenue, note 2); valued at Ukraine's recipients' consumption as the stand-in.

rows.label: Shelter: ln(consumption) gain per person over the years of use
rows.formula: pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, shl_years) * (shl_mic_share * ln(1 + shl_value_per_person / shl_years * cpi_2024_vs_2025 / ukr_consumption) + (1 - shl_mic_share) * ln(1 + shl_value_per_person / shl_years * cpi_2017_vs_2025 * ppp_factor / baseline_consumption))
rows.explainer: The value spread over its years of use, each year's log gain at the group's consumption, discounted at the shared rate.

rows.label: Shelter: share of the excess deaths the shelter averts among the people reached
rows.explainer: Judgment 1% (0.2-4%): no study measures what emergency shelter does to mortality (Maynard, Parker and Twigg 2017, Humanitarian Evidence Programme, rate the health evidence as limited); shelter, insulation and fuel protect against exposure in winter (Afghanistan, Ukraine, Syria, Gaza). Below ShelterBox's 2%, whose kits carry mosquito nets and water filters.

rows.label: Shelter: deaths averted per person reached (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Excess deaths over the time covered, times the share averted, in the low-income crises only.

rows.label: Shelter: episodes of acute illness averted per person reached
rows.explainer: The shared figure for shelter, blankets and site work (@humanitarian_response.shelter_illness_episodes_averted, 0.03, 0-0.1).

rows.label: Length of an episode of acute illness
rows.explainer: The shared length of an acute illness episode (@humanitarian_response.acute_illness_episode_years): about five days, three to eleven.

rows.label: Shelter: illness averted per person, in DALYs (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Episodes × their length × GBD's disability weight for a moderate acute infection.

rows.label: Education: learning gain of programmes for children in school or in light-touch activities (SD)

source.title: Evans & Yuan (2022), How Big Are Effect Sizes in International Education Studies?, Educational Evaluation and Policy Analysis, doi:10.3102/01623737221079646
source.quote: We identify a median effect size of 0.10 standard deviations on learning and 0.07 standard deviations on access among randomized controlled trials.

rows.explainer: The median effect on learning of randomised evaluations of education programmes in low- and middle-income countries, 0.10 SD, mostly programmes improving schooling children already attend; the range from light-touch activities such as short first-line learning spaces (0.03 SD) to well-run teacher-training and remedial programmes (0.2 SD). Used for the participants not in structured education for out-of-school children (edu_access_share). NRC publishes no controlled evaluation of its own; we found no published learning results from PRIO's randomised evaluation of NRC's accelerated education in Uganda (2019-21).

rows.label: Education: adult earnings gain per SD of skill still there in adult life
rows.explainer: The site's one figure for low- and middle-income countries (@education.earnings_gain_per_sd_adult_skills_lmic: 20%, 10% to 30%), from the Center for Global Development's review of the studies linking adults' reading and maths to their earnings, per SD of skill still there in adult life.

rows.label: Education: share of the learning gain still there in adult life
rows.explainer: The site's one figure (@education.test_gain_persistence_to_adulthood: 40%, 20% to 70%): test-score gains fade, a fifth to a half of a year's learning carrying into the next grade in Pakistan's schools (Andrabi and others 2011).

rows.label: Education: years until the children reach working age
rows.explainer: Judgment 10 years (6-15): mostly primary-age children, some youth in training (15-24) closer to work.

rows.label: Years the earnings gain lasts
rows.explainer: GiveWell's shared figure for long-term income gains (40 years).

rows.label: Household members sharing the earnings gain
rows.explainer: GiveWell's shared figure: an earner's gain is shared in the household.

rows.label: Education: share of participants in structured or accelerated education for children out of school
rows.explainer: Judgment 10% (5-25%): NRC's education counts mix accelerated and non-formal education that brings out-of-school children into learning for a school year (p. 18), with first-line learning spaces of a few weeks or months, Better Learning Programme sessions in public schools and teacher training (pp. 16-17); it publishes no split of the 1.29 million participants, and the accelerated programmes it describes are small (560 pupils in the DRC programme profiled on p. 18), so most participants are in the lighter activities.

rows.label: Education: learning gain of structured education for children otherwise out of school (SD)
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.5 SD (0.25-0.65): the randomised trial of village-based schools in Afghanistan (Burde and Linden 2013, American Economic Journal: Applied Economics 5(3)) found girls' test scores 0.65 and boys' 0.40 standard deviations higher ('their average test scores increase by 0.65 standard deviations', abstract, https://doi.org/10.1257/app.5.3.27) when schooling replaced none; 0.5 for a mix of girls and boys; NRC's accelerated programmes are shorter and its children more often move, so the low end is half that.

rows.label: Education: learning gain per participant, mixed (SD)
rows.explainer: Participants in structured education for out-of-school children at the access trial's gain; the rest (first-line spaces, sessions in schools, teacher training) at the median of education trials.

rows.label: Education: ln(consumption) gain per child, discounted
rows.formula: ln(1 + edu_gain_sd * edu_earnings_per_sd * edu_persistence) * pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, working_years) * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ (0 - edu_years_until_work) * resource_sharing_multiplier
rows.explainer: The yearly earnings gain over a working life, discounted to today from when work starts.

rows.label: Share of people in conflict-affected populations with a mental disorder
rows.explainer: The shared WHO prevalence in conflict-affected populations (@humanitarian_response.conflict_mental_disorder_prevalence, 22.1%, 18.8-25.7%); NRC's education and protection participants are displaced by conflict. Used for the Better Learning Programme and for protection.

rows.label: Average share of an initial gain kept over its years when it fades linearly to nothing
rows.explainer: A gain that falls in a straight line from its first size to zero averages half its first size over those years.

rows.label: Education: improvement in mental health from the Better Learning Programme for children with a disorder (SD)
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.1 SD (0-0.25): the Better Learning Programme is classroom psychosocial support in all NRC education programmes (p. 17); meta-analyses of school-based psychosocial programmes in humanitarian settings find small falls in post-traumatic stress and none consistent for depression (Purgato et al. 2018, Lancet Global Health), and this is a light, teacher-delivered version. Below the 0.2 SD of NRC's protection work.

rows.label: Education: years the psychosocial gain lasts
rows.explainer: Judgment half a year (3-12 months): the Better Learning Programme's sessions run over a school term or year, and follow-ups of classroom psychosocial programmes in conflict settings find most of the gain gone within months; low end a term, high end a school year. Fading linearly.

rows.label: Education: WELLBYs per child from psychosocial support
rows.explainer: Children with a disorder × the gain in SD × its years, fading linearly (linear_fade_share), × the shared WELLBYs per SD-year. Within a year, so not discounted.

rows.label: WASH: diarrhoeal deaths per person-year in the crisis sites
rows.explainer: The shared figure for crisis sites (@humanitarian_response.wash_crisis_diarrhoea_deaths_per_person_year, 0.0008, 0.0004-0.002); NRC's WASH work spans Gaza, Sudan, Yemen and the DRC, where it runs high, and Ukraine and Lebanon, where it runs low.

rows.label: WASH: fall in diarrhoeal deaths among the people served
rows.explainer: The shared figure for emergency WASH (@humanitarian_response.wash_crisis_diarrhoea_death_reduction, 15%, 3-35%).

rows.label: Other deaths averted per diarrhoeal death averted
rows.explainer: GiveWell's shared ratio for water treatment: deaths from other causes that diarrhoea makes more likely.

rows.label: WASH: years the service lasts per person reached
rows.explainer: Judgment a year (6 months to 3 years): water trucking and hygiene kits last months, repaired systems and latrines years.

rows.label: WASH: years of service, discounted
rows.explainer: Each year's benefit at the shared discount rate.

rows.label: WASH: value of a diarrhoeal death averted
rows.explainer: The site's age split of diarrhoeal deaths in Sub-Saharan Africa (facts/death_ages.json, WHO GHE) by the site's values by age.

rows.label: WASH: deaths averted per person served (before adjustments)
WASH: diarrhoea episodes averted per person-year of service
rows.explainer: The shared figure for emergency WASH (@humanitarian_response.wash_crisis_diarrhoea_episodes_averted, 0.1, 0.02-0.3).

rows.label: WASH: diarrhoea illness averted per person, in DALYs (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Episodes averted × their length × GBD's disability weight for moderate diarrhoea.

rows.label: WASH: value of water-fetching time saved, as a share of consumption
rows.explainer: The shared figure for time saved fetching water, mostly women's and girls' (@water.time_saved_consumption_share, 0.75% of consumption, 0-3%).

rows.label: WASH: ln(consumption) gain per person from time saved
Legal assistance: share of participants counselled or assisted on a legal problem
rows.explainer: The shared figure for displacement legal aid (@humanitarian_response.legal_aid_case_share, 30%, 15-50%): many of the 1.5 million get legal information in group sessions or online (KOBLI's platforms reached over 400,000, p. 20); the rest individual counselling, legal assistance or representation.

rows.label: Legal assistance: share of those cases resolved (document, legal stay, tenure secured)
rows.explainer: Judgment 50% (30-70%): NRC reports cases resolved for many of its clients (Jordan's civil documentation project, p. 21), but no outcome rate across countries; cases on housing, land and property and legal stay often stall.

rows.label: Legal assistance: consumption gain for a resolved case
rows.explainer: The shared figure for a resolved legal case (@humanitarian_response.legal_aid_consumption_gain, 5%, 1-15%).

rows.label: Legal assistance: years the gain lasts
rows.explainer: The shared figure (@humanitarian_response.legal_aid_years, 3 years, 1-6).

rows.label: Legal assistance: ln(consumption) gain per participant, discounted
rows.formula: icl_case_share * icl_resolved_share * ln(1 + icl_consumption_gain) * pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, icl_years)
rows.explainer: Only resolved cases count; information alone is counted at nothing here (its value is in unmodelled_benefits_adj).

rows.label: Protection: improvement in mental health for participants with a disorder (SD)
rows.explainer: The shared figure for broad protection work (@humanitarian_response.protection_mental_health_effect_sd, 0.2 SD, 0.05-0.4): NRC's protection is mostly community safety, mediation and site management, with case management for a few.

rows.label: Protection: years the gain lasts
rows.explainer: Judgment a year (6 months to 2 years), fading linearly; as Save the Children's protection branch.

rows.label: Protection: WELLBYs per participant
rows.explainer: Participants with a disorder × the gain in SD × its years, fading linearly (linear_fade_share), × the shared WELLBYs per SD-year. Participants without a disorder, and violence averted, are in unmodelled_benefits_adj.

rows.label: NORCAP: yearly programme budget an assignment's work shapes (US$)
rows.explainer: Judgment $2m ($0.5m-8m): a cluster coordinator, protection (ProCap) or gender (GenCap) adviser or cash expert (CashCap) shapes a country response of tens of millions shared with many staff; a technical expert in a ministry, the African Union or an energy or climate-services project a budget of a few million.

rows.label: NORCAP: improvement in that budget's value from the expert's work
rows.explainer: Judgment 5% (1-15%): better targeting, coordination and technical quality. Anchor: charityevals' Save the Children advocacy model takes 10% (3-30%) for research that changes practice; a secondee's effect is diluted across a whole response.

rows.label: NORCAP: value of a dollar of the supported work, as a multiple of cash to the poor
rows.explainer: The site's shared value of a dollar of humanitarian aid whose use isn't known more exactly (facts/aid_value.json): about a fifth of cash (0.05-0.8), what the site's relief models say relief does per dollar before their missing-data step, which this branch applies itself. The hosts' work is humanitarian response, coordination, protection, climate services, peace and elections; peace and governance work may be worth more or nothing.

rows.label: NORCAP: value of a dollar of the supported work (units of value)
NORCAP: units of value per assignment (before adjustments)
Evidence adjustment, food security
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.75 (0.5-1): the death share is a judgment without a trial, and part of the value (seeds, training, bakeries) depends on harvests and markets; as Save the Children's emergency branch.

rows.label: Share of the food security outcome others wouldn't have delivered
rows.explainer: Judgment 70% (45-90%): only 35% of the 2025 appeals' requirements were met, a shortfall of $30.5 billion, the largest in appeal history (ALNAP 2026), so others rarely fill the gap a responder leaves; in better-funded places more would have come anyway. Reference class: Save the Children's emergencies 65%, MSF's relief 72%.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, cash
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.9 (0.7-1): cash is valued at what recipients get, which trials of cash transfers support well (spent mostly on food and essentials, no rise in temptation goods); some doubt about transfers in fast-moving crises reaching who they should.

rows.label: Share of the cash outcome others wouldn't have delivered
rows.explainer: Judgment 70% (45-90%), as food security: the 2025 appeals were 35% funded (ALNAP 2026); in Ukraine the government and UN agencies also pay cash, but to fewer than need it.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, shelter
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.75 (0.5-1): the value of shelter is its cost to the household, but the health effects are judgments without trials (Maynard et al. 2017).

rows.label: Share of the shelter outcome others wouldn't have delivered
rows.explainer: Judgment 70% (45-90%), as food security: shelter clusters were among the least funded in 2025.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, education
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.6 (0.3-1): the learning gain mixes an access trial in Afghanistan and the median of other programmes' trials, the earnings link is from other settings, and displaced children move and drop out; as Save the Children's education branch.

rows.label: Share of the education outcome others wouldn't have delivered
rows.explainer: Judgment 85% (60-100%): most of the children would otherwise get no schooling (over half of refugee children are out of school, p. 16); some would join government or other NGOs' schools. As Save the Children's education branch.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, WASH
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.65 (0.4-1): the fall in deaths rests on meta-analyses of household water and sanitation trials, not on emergency delivery, and on a judged crisis death rate.

rows.label: Share of the WASH outcome others wouldn't have delivered
rows.explainer: Judgment 70% (45-90%), as food security: water in camps is often a single provider's, but the WASH cluster can reassign it.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, legal assistance
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.5 (0.3-0.9): no study measures what legal assistance does for displaced people's consumption; resolution rates are NRC's own reports.

rows.label: Share of the legal assistance outcome others wouldn't have delivered
rows.explainer: Judgment 85% (60-100%): few others give displaced people legal assistance; some would resolve their case alone or through UNHCR's partners.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, protection
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.6 (0.3-0.9): the effect is a judgment from psychosocial trials of more focused programmes; as Save the Children's protection branch.

rows.label: Share of the protection outcome others wouldn't have delivered
rows.explainer: Judgment 85% (60-100%): protection services for those outside mainstream programmes are scarce; Save the Children's protection branch takes 90%.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, NORCAP
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.6 (0.3-1): the budget and improvement are judgments; secondees' value is reported by the hosts, not measured.

rows.label: Share of the NORCAP outcome others wouldn't have delivered
rows.explainer: Judgment 50% (20-80%): host agencies would fill some posts themselves, by their own recruitment or through the other standby partners' rosters (the UN agencies keep agreements with a dozen or more), often later or with less experienced staff; posts in new or neglected emergencies are hardest to fill.

rows.label: NRC's share of the resources behind the relief outcomes (food security, cash, shelter, WASH)
rows.explainer: Judgment 90% (75-100%): NRC delivers most work itself with its donors' money, which is in its accounts (UN agencies' grants included); local partners and communities add labour and some goods in kind, and in-kind pipelines (WFP food, UNICEF supplies) handled but not booked add a little.

rows.label: Share of credit used, relief branches
rows.explainer: NRC's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: NRC's share of the resources behind the education outcome
rows.explainer: Judgment 80% (60-100%): governments supply schools and some teachers, and NRC trains them; NRC pays most of what its programmes need. As Save the Children's education branch.

rows.label: NRC's share of the resources behind the legal assistance outcome
rows.explainer: Judgment 80% (60-100%): the authorities issue the documents and courts decide; NRC's lawyers do the work that gets the case there.

rows.label: NRC's share of the resources behind the protection outcome
rows.explainer: Judgment 85% (60-100%): communities' own time and local authorities share in mediation and safety work.

rows.label: NRC's share of the resources behind the NORCAP outcome
rows.explainer: Judgment 60% (30-90%): the improvement is made by the host's team and budget with the expert; NRC pays the expert.

rows.label: Delivery adjustment (participants who get the service as modelled)
rows.explainer: Judgment 85% (70-95%), every branch: the reach is NRC's own count, with donors' audits and third-party monitoring of many projects; some participants are counted twice within a line or get only a light touch, and some aid is delayed, diverted or lost in conflict (Sudan, Gaza, Myanmar). Reference class: 85% for Save the Children's and MSF's relief.

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: 1 (0.85-1.1): 91% of NRC's income is restricted grants from governments and the UN; a private gift (8%) co-funds grants, starts responses before grants arrive and pays for what grants don't cover, and can't be told apart from them. No sign it pulls in more or is displaced.

rows.label: Missing-data discount, food security
rows.explainer: Thin: people reached is NRC's count, but the share of deaths averted and the value delivered are judgments with no trial of NRC's work. So it is counted less by the shared slider, the same way in every model (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: Missing-data discount, cash (the transfers)
rows.explainer: Measured: the cash is valued at what people receive, NRC's own count of the 1.8 million people reached meets the money it reports transferring (NOK 1,425m, p. 30), and valuing cash at face value needs no effect study (as charityevals' American Red Cross model's assistance). The judged part of the branch, its deaths averted, takes the slider in csh_judged_missing_data_adj.

rows.label: Missing-data discount, cash (deaths averted)
rows.explainer: Thin: the share of excess deaths cash averts is a judgment with no study of NRC's work. So they are counted less by the shared slider, the same way in every model (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: Missing-data discount, shelter
rows.explainer: Thin: the health effects and the years of use are judgments, with no study of NRC's shelter. So it is counted less by the shared slider, the same way in every model (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: Missing-data discount, education
rows.explainer: Thin: the learning gain is other programmes' median, with no controlled evaluation of NRC's. So it is counted less by the shared slider, the same way in every model (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: Missing-data discount, WASH
rows.explainer: Thin: the fall in deaths is from household trials of other delivery, not emergency WASH. So it is counted less by the shared slider, the same way in every model (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: Missing-data discount, legal assistance
rows.explainer: Thin: the resolution rate and the gain per case are judgments. So it is counted less by the shared slider, the same way in every model (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: Missing-data discount, protection
rows.explainer: Thin: the effect is a judgment from other programmes' trials. So it is counted less by the shared slider, the same way in every model (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: Missing-data discount, NORCAP
rows.explainer: Thin: the budget shaped and the improvement are judgments. So it is counted less by the shared slider, the same way in every model (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: Benefits and harms not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Not modelled, with signs: legal information and protection's gains for people without a disorder or a resolved case, violence averted by mediation and site management, livelihoods' income in later years, NRC's coordination roles (170+ inter-agency leaders, p. 41) and the Emergency Response Section's surge deployments (+); tension between displaced and host communities, and funging inside the response (-; aid diverted in conflict is in implementation_adj). Judgment +5% (-10% to +20%), as Save the Children's.
